models_evaluated: Zero-Trust Data Sanitization (ZTDS) client-side de-identification engine

links.outcome: PHI detection recall and latency of client-side de-identification before LLM API transmission, versus cloud DLP proxy
links.effect: ZTDS achieved 99.94% recall on direct HIPAA 18 identifiers with 1.84 ms latency per note, versus 242.6 ms for cloud DLP proxy; zero outbound PHI bytes in network packet inspection.
links.quote: In a benchmark evaluation across 2,500 synthetic multi-center clinical notes containing dense, co-occurring PHI entities (names, medical record numbers, dates, geographic subdivisions, biometricidentifiers, device identifiers, and contact vectors), the client-side ZTDS engine achieved a 99.94% recall rate on direct HIPAA 18 identifiers with an average processing latency of 1.84 ms per standard clinicalnote (mean length: 1,420 characters).

unlisted_practices: Client-side ephemeral de-identification with local token re-identification session dictionary before sending text to third-party AI APIs, as a route to avoid Business Associate status

screen.practice: client-side de-identification before sending text to LLM APIs
screen.reason: The study develops and empirically benchmarks a client-side ephemeral de-identification / data sanitization safeguard to prevent PHI exfiltration when sending clinical text to cloud-hosted LLM APIs.
